summary.headline: Planning Board approves modifications for 22 and 154 Turnpike Road, schedules additional November meeting for Costco review.
summary.summary: The Planning Board approved site plan modifications for the golf driving range at 22 Turnpike Road and the Chase Bank development at 154 Turnpike Road. Hearings for the 21 Coslin Drive Costco proposal and the Fay School building addition as-built review were continued to November 2. The board also reviewed preliminary benchmarking and strategy for updating the town's Master Plan for 2030 and discussed the 2027 meeting calendar.

topics.title: 22 Turnpike Road major site plan modification
topics.summary: The board reviewed a draft decision approving modifications to the major site plan for the golf driving range at 22 Turnpike Road. Discussion centered on confirming lighting fixture limits, internal timing controls, and stormwater infiltration test pit requirements to verify separation from groundwater during construction.
key_details: Applicant representative Peter Bemis agreed that test pits could be conducted as part of the bottom inspection during construction.
Exterior lighting must comply with outdoor illumination bylaws, using fixtures not exceeding 3,000 Kelvin except as identified on approved lighting plans.
The board closed the twelfth public hearing on the modification before taking a vote to approve the decision.
topics.outcome: Public hearing closed and site plan modification approved 4-0 (with Tom Truong abstaining).

topics.title: 154 Turnpike Road major site plan modification
topics.summary: The board reviewed a modification decision for 154 Turnpike Road, represented by Capital Group Properties for the Chase Bank location. The conditions addressed site lighting controls, dimming adjustments for non-compliant fixtures, landscaping maintenance, accessible parking layout, and as-built plan submissions.
key_details: Light fixtures originally installed exceeded 3,000 Kelvin but were fitted with internal timers and electronic dimmers to meet illumination standards.
The applicant clarified that accessible parking spaces remained in their existing location rather than being re-striped to a new location.
The applicant agreed to provide revised plans with Planning Board endorsement blocks and complete as-builts.
topics.outcome: Public hearing closed and site plan modification approved 4-0 (with Tom Truong abstaining).

topics.title: 21 Coslin Drive Costco hearing continuation and schedule
topics.summary: The board considered procedural continuations for the Costco applications at 21 Coslin Drive, which include major site plan approval and special permits for Highway Major Retail and Lower Impact Development. Because peer review traffic studies were still under preparation, the board voted to schedule a special meeting on November 2, 2026, and extend the statutory decision deadline.
key_details: The Costco traffic study and consultant peer review were not ready for presentation.
The board scheduled a special meeting on November 2, 2026, at 6:30 PM to take up Costco and avoid overcrowding the mid-November agenda.
The statutory deadline for the board to act on the major site plan application was formally extended to December 18, 2026.
topics.outcome: Hearing continued to November 2, 2026 at 6:30 PM (5-0 vote); decision deadline extended to December 18, 2026 (5-0 vote).
topics.why_it_matters: Costco is one of the largest commercial developments proposed in Southborough, drawing significant community interest regarding traffic, infrastructure, and site layout.

topics.title: Fay School building addition landscape and as-built review
topics.summary: Fay School representatives presented their version 3 landscape mitigation plan and requested review of as-built compliance for their primary school building addition. The board reviewed favorable comments from the town's native plant consultant but decided to wait for Fuss and O'Neill's engineering review before approving the as-built and occupancy sign-off.
key_details: Fay School's native plant mitigation plan was reviewed and praised by native plant consultant Freddie Gillespie.
The town's engineering consultant, Fuss and O'Neill, experienced a work queue backlog and anticipated delivering their follow-up review later in the week.
The applicant noted that their temporary certificate of occupancy expires on November 19, 2026.
The matter was set to be taken up again at the board's newly scheduled November 2, 2026 meeting.

topics.title: Master Plan 2030 planning and implementation committee update
topics.summary: Members of the Master Plan Implementation Committee presented a slide deck and benchmarking study on how neighboring towns structure and fund master plan updates. The presentation highlighted lessons learned from the 2021 plan, proposing to consolidate hundreds of separate actions into roughly 50 priority themes and exploring hiring a light-touch consultant to guide town volunteers.
key_details: Roughly 15 percent of the 2021 Master Plan's 200-plus goals are complete, with most others in process.
Nearby towns paid between $18,000 and $130,000 for consultant assistance, with full private consultant proposals running upwards of $125,000 to $250,000.
The committee suggested forming a 15-member subcommittee in 2027 to seek technical assistance grants and prepare for a potential FY28 or FY29 funding request.
Board members cautioned that municipal budget constraints and a potential Proposition 2 1/2 override could make Town Meeting appropriations difficult, emphasizing the need for state grants.
topics.outcome: No formal action taken; the board will place the Master Plan strategy on a future agenda.

topics.title: 2027 Planning Board meeting schedule
topics.summary: The board reviewed a draft 2027 meeting calendar. Members discussed potential gaps between meetings in March and the fall, recommending the addition of second meetings in February, March, and November to accommodate heavy project loads.
key_details: Members raised concerns that having only one meeting in February and a three-week gap in March would cause late-night meetings.
Staff will adjust the proposed dates to balance the schedule around holidays and bring a revised draft back on November 2, 2026.
topics.outcome: Staff directed to revise the calendar for review at the November 2, 2026 meeting.

topics.title: Planner's report and routine business
topics.summary: The town planner reported on recent Town Meeting zoning results, upcoming meetings, site plan compliance enforcement, tree planting requirements, and FY28 budget preparations. The board also approved meeting minutes from September 28, 2026, and executive session minutes from June 4, 2026 for format only.
key_details: The Select Board's next regular meeting was moved to Wednesday, November 4, 2026.
The Southborough Historical Society's attorney submitted a letter seeking to withdraw their zoning appeal for 40-42 Central Street ahead of the October 21 ZBA hearing.
Town Counsel advised that the special permit for 250 Turnpike Road had been legally exercised through pre-construction and recording activities.
The preliminary FY28 Planning Board operating budget reflects an approximate $8,000 increase primarily driven by contractual salary steps and cost-of-living adjustments.
topics.outcome: Routine reports accepted and minutes approved.

votes.motion: To close the public hearing for the 22 Turnpike Road modification to major site plan approval.
To approve the decision for the 22 Turnpike Road modification to major site plan approval for the golf driving range.
To close the public hearing on the 154 Turnpike Road modification to major site plan approval.
To approve the decision for the 154 Turnpike Road modification to major site plan approval.
To continue the public hearing for 21 Coslin Drive (Costco) to November 2, 2026 at 6:30 PM.
To extend the decision due date for the 21 Coslin Drive (Costco) major site plan approval application to December 18, 2026.

public_comment.summary: A resident asked whether the public would have an opportunity at a later date to ask questions about the scope of the consultant peer reviews for the 21 Coslin Drive Costco project. The chair confirmed that peer reviews will be presented and discussed on November 2, 2026, and that written comments may be submitted to the town planner in advance.
